The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Retreat

What is the doh of Retreat?

In this version, in C major, doh is C. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Retreat start on?

It starts on m (E in C major), a pickup before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

What words can be sung to Retreat?

Retreat is in the metre 8.8.8.8 — Long Metre (L.M.): lines of 8, 8, 8, 8 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it, such as 'Take Up Thy Cross', the Savior Said, 'Tis by the Faith of Joys to Come, 'Tis from the Treasures of His Word; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Retreat in the public domain?

Yes. Thomas Hastings died in 1872; the tune was first published in 1842. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
